parole.testo: According to Georgiev, possibly of Oghur origin, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *ȫrük (“tangle, knit”), whence Turkish örgü (“knit”).

parole.significato: thick rug, blanket (typically used as a covering for bed, coach; occasionally as tapestry for wall)
parole.testo: Perhaps of Oghur origin, from Proto-Turkic *köbüŕ (“rug”). Mladenov alternatively theoretizes possible origin from dialectal гу́ба (gúba, “enfolding, wrapping”) + -ер (-er), although suffix -ер (-er) typically yields agent nouns rather than instrumentals.

Оf Oghur or Kipchak (probably Pecheneg) origin, from Proto-Turkic *tajak (“staff”). Cognate with Chuvash туя (tuja), Tatar таяк (tayaq), Turkish dayak.
Of Oghur origin, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *siāŕgan (“carp, dragon”). Cognate with Turkish sazan (“carp”) and Hungarian sárkány (“dragon”), an Oghur borrowing.

parole.significato: year-old lamb (whose teeth have grown and has stopped breastfeeding)
parole.testo: Probably of Oghur origin from Proto-Turkic *sīĺ (“wedge, tooth”) + -е (-e) (diminutive suffix). Compare Serbo-Croatian шѝљег (“male lamb”) (dialectal). Akin to the Turkish borrowing Bulgarian шиш (šiš, “skewer”) (Turkish şiş), Chuvash шӑл (šăl, “tooth”).
Possibly of Oghur origin, akin to Proto-Turkic *sǖb- (“wedge, thorn”) + -ак (-ak).
